data.formatContent:
The 2003 NHL Draft Lottery was used to determine the order of selection for the first 14 picks in the first round of the 2003 NHL Draft. It consisted of one drawing, with the winning team able to move up a maximum of four positions in the draft order. 

The 14 teams that did not qualify for the 2003 Stanley Cup Playoffs – or the teams that acquired the first-round picks of those non-playoff teams – participated in the lottery and were assigned odds based on inverse order of regular-season points. The only clubs with the opportunity to receive the first overall selection were the five teams with the lowest regular-season point totals, or the clubs that acquired an eligible club’s first-round draft pick.

Fourteen balls, numbered 1 to 14, were placed in a lottery machine. The machine randomly expelled four balls. The resulting four-number series (without regard to selection order) was matched against a chart that showed all possible combinations and the clubs to which each was assigned.

The 13 teams not selected in the lottery were assigned draft selections based on the result of the drawing, moving down a maximum of one position.

The 2003 NHL Draft Lottery was held Monday, April 7, at the NHL’s New York office.

data.formatContent:
The 1999 NHL Draft Lottery was used to determine the order of selection for the first 12 picks in the first round of the 1999 NHL Draft. It consisted of one drawing, with the winning team able to move up a maximum of four positions in the draft order. 

Participants included the expansion Atlanta Thrashers and all teams that did not qualify for the 1999 Stanley Cup Playoffs (or the teams that acquired the first-round picks of those non-playoff teams). The Thrashers entered the lottery with the same odds as the team finishing the regular season with the second-worst record. The only clubs with the opportunity to receive the first overall selection were the four teams with the lowest regular-season point totals (or the clubs that acquired an eligible club’s first-round draft pick), plus Atlanta.

Fourteen balls, numbered 1 to 14, were placed in a lottery machine. The machine randomly expelled four balls. The resulting four-number series (without regard to selection order) was matched against a chart that showed all possible combinations and the clubs to which each was assigned.

The 11 teams not selected in the lottery were assigned draft selections based on the result of the drawing, moving down a maximum of one position.

The 1999 NHL Draft Lottery was held Sunday, May 16, at the NHL’s New York office.

data.formatContent:
The 2021 NHL Draft Lottery was used to determine the order of selection for the first 16 picks in the first round of the 2021 NHL Draft. It consisted of two drawings: the 1st Lottery Draw determined the team selecting first overall, the 2nd Lottery Draw determined the team selecting second overall.

Participants in the Draft Lottery included the expansion Seattle Kraken and all teams that did not qualify for the 2021 Stanley Cup Playoffs (or the teams that acquired the first-round picks of those non-playoff teams). Each participating club had the chance to win the first overall selection.

The Kraken entered the Draft Lottery as the No. 3 seed and owning the exact same lottery odds as the No. 4 seed (the team finishing the regular season with the third-worst regular-season record), mirroring the status of the Vegas Golden Knights entering their inaugural Draft Lottery participation in 2017. The Kraken were guaranteed no lower than the fifth overall selection.

To accommodate the addition of a 16th team in the Draft Lottery, the odds for all other participating teams were reduced proportionally from the odds used in 2020.

Fourteen balls, numbered 1 to 14, were placed in a lottery machine. The machine randomly expelled four balls. The resulting four-number series (without regard to selection order) was matched against a chart that showed all possible combinations and the clubs to which each was assigned.

The 2021 NHL Draft Lottery was held Wednesday, June 2, at NHL Network’s Secaucus, N.J., studio.

data.formatContent:
The 2020 NHL Draft Lottery was used to determine the order of selection for the first 15 picks in the 2020 NHL Draft. As a result of a pause in the 2019-20 regular season due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the lottery was held in two phases, with Phase 2 necessary only based on Phase 1 results.

Phase 1 – There were three drawings in Phase 1: the 1st Lottery Draw determined the team selecting first overall, the 2nd Lottery Draw determined the team selecting second overall and the 3rd Lottery Draw determined the team selecting third overall. Fifteen teams were eligible: the seven teams that did not resume play in 2019-20 – ranked in inverse order of their points percentages at the time of the pause in the regular season – and eight “placeholders” that represent the to-be-determined teams that did not advance through the 2020 Stanley Cup Qualifiers (or the teams that acquired their first-round picks). This maintained previously established odds for the Draft Lottery. Each participating club had the chance to win the first overall selection.

Fourteen balls, numbered 1 to 14, were placed in a lottery machine. The machine randomly expelled four balls. The resulting four-number series (without regard to selection order) was matched against a chart that showed all possible combinations and the clubs to which each was assigned.

The 1st Lottery Draw, 2nd Lottery Draw and 3rd Lottery Draw determined the right to the first, second and third overall pick, respectively. For each draw, if the winning team was from the #1-7 group (teams that did not resume play), that team won the right to the corresponding pick. If the winning team was from the #8-15 group (teams eliminated during the Stanley Cup Qualifiers), the right to the respective pick would be determined in Phase 2.

After each Lottery Draw, the winning team (from either group of teams) was no longer eligible for ensuing draws. All number combinations originally assigned to that team became “Re-Draw Combinations” for ensuing draws and the remaining teams’ odds increased on a proportionate basis based on which teams won previous draws.

In Phase 1, one of the eight placeholders – ‘Team E’ – won the 1st Lottery Draw, yielding the requirement of Phase 2. The other draws in Phase 1 were won by the Los Angeles Kings (2nd Lottery Draw) and Ottawa Senators (3rd Lottery Draw; with a position previously acquired in a trade with the San Jose Sharks), thereby locking in the order of selection for picks 2-8.

Phase 2 – There was one Lottery Draw in Phase 2, used to determine the first overall pick in the 2020 NHL Draft. Each of the eight teams eliminated from the 2020 Stanley Cup Qualifiers participated, receiving the same odds (12.5%) and represented in the lottery machine by one ball with their team logo – all eligible to claim the No. 1 pick. The seven teams not selected in Phase 2, in inverse order of their points percentages at the time of the pause in the regular season, were assigned draft positions 9 through 15.


Phase 1 of the 2020 NHL Draft Lottery was conducted Friday, June 26, at NHL Network’s Secaucus, N.J., studio. Phase 2 took place at the same location, Monday, Aug. 10.
